title: Paging, Filtering, and Sorting a List Endpoint

contentBlocks.body: A list endpoint is where a CRUD API usually gets slow or leaky. Treat every query-string value as untrusted input: give `page` and `pageSize` defaults and clamp them (a client asking for 100,000 rows should get 100), trim filters and treat blanks as no filter, and build the query with `IQueryable` so filtering, sorting and paging all run in SQL rather than in memory.

Sort from an allowlist. Mapping `sort=price` or `sort=-created` to a known expression is safe; building an `OrderBy` from any property name the client sends lets them sort by columns they should not see, and string-built SQL is an injection risk. Always finish with a unique tie-breaker such as `Id`. Without it, rows with equal prices can come back in a different order on each request, so a row can appear on two pages or on none.

Offset paging with a total count is right for admin grids where users jump to page 7. For infinite scroll or large, fast-changing tables, prefer keyset pagination from the query-performance lesson: it stays fast on deep pages and does not skip or repeat rows when data changes.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Why must a sorted list endpoint end its ORDER BY with a unique column such as Id?

choices: Without it, rows with equal sort values can change order between requests and appear on two pages or none
SQL requires every ORDER BY to include the primary key
It makes the query use less memory
It hides the Id from the client
payload.answer: Without it, rows with equal sort values can change order between requests and appear on two pages or none
payload.explanation: The database may return ties in any order. A unique tie-breaker makes the order total, so page boundaries are stable.

knowledgeItems.prompt: A client sends `?sort=PasswordHash`. What should a well-built list endpoint do?

choices: Sort by PasswordHash, since the client asked for it
Ignore it and use the default sort, because only allowlisted fields are sortable
Build the ORDER BY clause from the string
Return 500 so the client stops trying
payload.answer: Ignore it and use the default sort, because only allowlisted fields are sortable
payload.explanation: Sorting by arbitrary columns leaks information (sort order reveals values) and dynamic SQL invites injection. Map known names to known expressions. Returning 400 is also reasonable; sorting by it is not.

payload.text: Never trust the requested page size: give it a default and ____ it to a maximum such as 100.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Implement GET /products with search and category filters, an allowlisted sort with an Id tie-breaker, clamped paging, and totals.
